skill.name: google-drive-automation
skill.description: Guides Google Drive automation through OAuth-based local commands for search, listing, downloads, uploads, and file organization.
skill.summary: Run Google Drive search, download, upload, and organization workflows from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick and Google Drive URL examples are mostly false positives, but several documented Python command flows are real external command execution. The larger risk is semantic: the skill requests broad Google Drive read/write operations, references scripts that are absent from the analyzed package, and describes opaque OAuth token refresh behavior.

remediation.issue: Referenced Python automation scripts are not included in the analyzed package.
remediation.suggestion: Ship the scripts with the skill and make them auditable, or remove executable command instructions until the scripts are available for review.

remediation.issue: Drive write commands can modify or trash user files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before upload, move, copy, rename, or trash operations, and document least-privilege OAuth scopes.

remediation.issue: OAuth token refresh depends on an unspecified cloud function.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact refresh endpoint and source code, or replace remote refresh behavior with a transparent local OAuth flow.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Google Drive Read and Write Access
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly describes full read/write Drive access and documents commands for uploads, moves, copies, renames, and trash operations. These workflows can expose or alter user Drive content if run without clear confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The capability statement and write command section directly document broad Drive access and destructive operations.

semantic_findings.title: Referenced Automation Scripts Not Present
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to run scripts/auth.py and scripts/drive.py, but the analyzed package contains only SKILL.md. Agents may fail or run unrelated local files with those paths if the working directory contains them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source repeatedly references local Python scripts, while the scanned file tree for this package includes no script files.

semantic_findings.title: Opaque OAuth Token Refresh Path
semantic_findings.description: The token management section says expired tokens are refreshed using a cloud function without naming the endpoint or providing source code. OAuth refresh behavior should be transparent because it can affect sensitive Drive credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation clearly mentions token storage and automatic cloud-function refresh, but the exact implementation is not visible in the analyzed package.

content.value_statement: Manual Drive file tasks slow down team workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Drive search, download, upload, and organization commands.
actual_capabilities: Documents OAuth login, status, and logout commands for Google Drive access.
Provides Drive search examples for full text, titles, URLs, shared files, and pagination.
Shows commands to list folders and download regular files by Drive ID.
Shows write commands for uploads, folder creation, moves, copies, renames, and trash operations.
Explains supported query formats, Drive ID sources, download limits, and token storage behavior.
limitations: The analyzed package contains only SKILL.md; referenced Python scripts are not present.
Requires a Google Workspace account and does not support personal Gmail accounts.
Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides cannot be downloaded directly through the documented tool.
Drive operations require local authentication and the user permissions available to that account.

use_cases.title: Find Team Documents
use_cases.description: Search Drive by text, title, shared status, URL, or folder ID, then identify the correct file for the task.

use_cases.title: Organize Workspace Files
use_cases.description: Create folders, move files, rename items, and copy documents after confirming the intended destination.

use_cases.title: Retrieve Reference Files
use_cases.description: List folder contents and download regular files needed for analysis, reporting, or review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Check Drive Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Google Drive automation skill to check whether I am authenticated. Explain any required next step before running a command.

prompt_templates.title: Search and Download
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my Drive for the file named [file name]. Show the likely matches, ask me to choose one, then download it to [local folder].

prompt_templates.title: Organize Folder Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the folder named [folder name]. List its contents and suggest which files should be moved or renamed before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Targeted Drive Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for files matching [criteria]. Prepare a proposed cleanup plan with file IDs, actions, and risks. Wait for approval before changing Drive.

output_examples.input: Search for quarterly report files and identify the newest one.
output_examples.output: Found several matching files. The newest likely match is Q4 Report.pdf in the Finance folder, based on its name and modified date.

output_examples.input: Create a project folder and move selected files into it.
output_examples.output: Prepared a move plan with the target folder and selected files. Confirmation is required before any Drive write operation runs.

output_examples.input: Download the selected PDF to my local downloads folder.
output_examples.output: The selected regular file can be downloaded locally. Workspace-native documents need export handling instead of direct download.

best_practices: Confirm file IDs, folder IDs, and destination paths before running any write command.
Ask for explicit approval before uploads, moves, copies, renames, or trash operations.
Use narrow search terms and least-privilege account access for sensitive Drive content.
anti_patterns: Running write or trash commands without user confirmation.
Assuming a Google Drive URL always points to the intended file or folder.
Trying to directly download Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides as regular files.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Google Workspace account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documentation says personal Gmail accounts are not supported.

faq.question: Does the analyzed package include the Python scripts?
faq.answer: No. The analyzed package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced scripts were not available for audit.

faq.question: Can it change files in Google Drive?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include upload, move, copy, rename, folder creation, and trash operations.

faq.question: Can it download Google Docs or Sheets directly?
faq.answer: No. The documentation says Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides require export or dedicated tools.

faq.question: Where are OAuth tokens stored?
faq.answer: The documentation says tokens are stored in the system keyring, such as Keychain, Credential Locker, or Secret Service.

faq.question: Should I approve Drive write actions manually?
faq.answer: Yes. Review file IDs, destinations, and the exact action before approving any write command.
